title: Interleaved NDJSON healer and backfill guide for mid-stream truncation
creator: Amira Patel
description: When clients receive partially truncated NDJSON streams (interleaved objects and toolcall markers) they often cannot safely resume or repair the stream. This ticket defines a server-side "healer" flow and a deterministic backfill manifest format that enables safe client resume, minimal client complexity, and repeatable post-hoc repairs for truncated responses.
problem_statement: Large streaming responses can be interrupted by network glitches, proxy timeouts, or server-side OOM. Currently clients either discard partial responses or attempt ad-hoc repairs. This yields inconsistent behavior across SDKs, toolcalls get duplicated or lost, and structured outputs become invalid JSON causing downstream failures in parsers and tool executors.
proposal_summary: 1) Emit a compact stream manifest header (base64 checksum + sequence markers + optional continuation token) at the start of long responses. 2) When truncation is detected, server retains a short-lived repair snapshot indexed by manifest id for a configurable TTL. 3) Clients may POST a resume request with manifest id and last-seen byte/line; server returns a deterministic repair segment (minimal suffix) that leads to a valid NDJSON sequence. 4) For interleaved toolcalls, tool-boundary sentinel records will be included in the manifest to guarantee idempotency when replaying tool calls.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Server snapshot retention increases memory/metadata surface and requires TTL/garbage collection tuning
Adding manifest header slightly increases response size and requires SDK parsing logic
Replay semantics for toolcalls need strict idempotency guarantees; not all external tools are idempotent
Edge cases around very large outputs where computing checksums is expensive—we'll use streaming rolling-hash to mitigate
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (JS/Python/Go) can parse manifest header and perform resume flow end-to-end in integration tests
Repair snapshots are stored and GC'd per TTL; snapshot store metrics visible in Console
No duplicated tool invocations observed in canary run (dedupe by toolcall sentinel + manifest id)
End-to-end latency regression <2% in 95th percentile for responses with manifest header enabled
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Define manifest binary/text format and streaming rolling checksum algorithm (this ticket)
Phase 2: Implement server manifest emitter + short-lived snapshot store behind an opt-in flag
Phase 3: Add resume endpoint and deterministic repair generator
Phase 4: SDK changes and canary with runtime-1.20; telemetry and dashboards
Phase 5: Turn on by default with rollout policy and monitoring-based rollback
test_plan: Unit tests for rolling checksum and manifest parsing
Fuzz truncated stream inputs and verify repair segment produces valid NDJSON
Integration test against toolcall sandbox to assert single invocation semantics
Load test to ensure snapshot store scales and GC behaves under churn
rollout_and_observability: Canary to 5% of hosted API requests with label 'manifest-canary'
Postmortem runbook link included in links
